62.0.0.en: 1- Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.

62.0.1.en: 1- Despite the severity of the affliction David suffered, being driven from the face of Absalom and threatened with death, his faith in God his Savior did not waver. He lifted his eyes toward Him, awaiting His salvation; indeed he waited upon God alone, as the verse means in the original Hebrew.

62.0.2.en: 2- Here David prophesies of Christ, the only Savior of all humanity, apart from whom there is no salvation, by his saying, "from him cometh my salvation."

62.1.0.en: 2- He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.

62.1.1.en: 1- David feels that God is his refuge, and he likens Him to the firm, strong rock; and so, since David held fast to God the Rock, he stood firm in his faith. Although at the beginning he was a little disturbed, his hope was to return to his place in Jerusalem. However strong a man may be, he is weak and liable to be disturbed. The beautiful thing is to see David's clinging to God: his disturbance did not last, and he felt God his Savior with him.

62.2.0.en: 3- How long will you attack a man? You all destroy him like a leaning wall, like a falling fence!

62.2.1.en: Leaning wall: a wall that is collapsing.

62.2.2.en: 1- David addresses his enemies and says to them: How long will you attack the man and try to shatter him like a wall, or a broken or collapsing fence? The man here means David, and this shows the extent of David's suffering, so that he was shaken a little (v. 2); at the same time it shows the extent of his faith in God who steadies him, so that all his enemies cannot prevail against him.

62.2.3.en: 2- The man also means Christ, against whom all rose up, Romans and Jews, rulers and people; yet He bore all this for our sake and died on the cross, but by the power of His divinity He rose from the dead.

62.2.4.en: 3- The enemies here signify the demons, who attack the spiritual person and try to demolish him, so that he suffers afflictions in his life and may fall into some sins; but through repentance God raises him up from them.

62.3.0.en: 4- They only consult to cast him down from his excellency: they delight in lies: they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah.

62.3.1.en: 1- David continues to describe what the wicked do to the righteous man: they try to turn him away from faithfulness and from the worship of God. This is the excellency, and they do this because they are children of the devil, so they love evil and hate good; therefore they try to remove righteous David from his righteousness.

62.3.2.en: 2- In addition to this, the wicked cast false accusations at the righteous man, and they delight in this because they are liars and also hypocrites. They bless the righteous man with kind words, but in their hearts they curse him and revile him. So did Absalom and Shimei the son of Gera to David.

62.3.3.en: 3- The righteous man is also Christ, whom the Jews tried to ensnare with a word, to make Him fall into error, and whom they charged with false accusations. They showed Him affection while their hearts wanted to kill Him, as Judas Iscariot did with Him, who betrayed Him with a kiss.

62.3.4.en: 4- This verse ends with the word "Selah," which is a musical pause for meditating on the hideousness of evil, so that a person may keep away from it.

62.3.5.en: Walk in goodness and do virtue, holding fast to God's commandments, for this is a proof of your sonship to Him. Keep away from evil so that you may not be a son of the devil. The more you love righteousness and strive toward it, the more your heart is filled with peace, and an inexpressible happiness awaits you in the Kingdom.

62.4.0.en: 5- My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.

62.4.1.en: In answer to all the plots of the wicked against David, we find that he does not speak with them, but speaks to himself, calling upon his soul to submit to God, to bear these sufferings from the wicked, and to wait for the Lord, its hope. This means two things:

62.4.2.en: 1- David's surrender of himself to God, his reliance on Him, and his acceptance of all sufferings for His sake.

62.4.3.en: 2- His faith and hope in God, who will surely intervene and rescue him from the hands of his enemies, and this is what indeed happened, for God restored David to his throne.

62.5.0.en: 6- He only is my rock and my salvation: he is my defence; I shall not be moved. 7- In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.

62.5.2.en: a- My rock: so he relies on Him, because the rock is firm and strong.

62.5.3.en: b- My salvation: for he has no deliverer from all his enemies and his afflictions except God, who is able to do all things.

62.5.4.en: c- My refuge: so he takes shelter in Him and is fortified against all the plots and attacks of the wicked.

62.5.5.en: d- My glory: for God does not only protect me, but also gives me glories that I taste in part on earth, and then fully in eternity.

62.5.6.en: 2- At the beginning of the psalm David declared that he was shaken only a little (v. 2), but after he trusted in God, placed his hope in Him and felt that He was his rock, he became firm and never shaken.

62.6.0.en: 8- Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.

62.6.1.en: 1- David sums up his counsels to the children of God who believe in Him in three matters:

62.6.2.en: a- Trust in God: for He is the only support in life, and trusting in Him is not only in time of affliction but at all times, so that a person lives secure from the enemy's attacks, open and hidden.

62.6.3.en: b- Pour out your heart: that is, pray with contrition and supplication to God, that He may intervene in one's life. Pouring out also means emptying the heart of every sin and worldly concern, that is, repentance, so that the heart becomes pure and ready to be filled with God.

62.6.4.en: c- Take refuge in Him: for He is the strong fortress inside which a person is secure and in which he remains always, in order to live in security.

62.6.5.en: 2- This verse ends with the word "Selah," which is a musical pause calling us to think about God, our hope, in whom we trust.

62.6.6.en: If only you would accustom yourself to prayer every day. Then your feelings will stir toward God and you will trust in Him, as you feel His power with you, and your heart will rejoice and be filled with His grace that overflows upon you.

62.7.0.en: 9- Surely the sons of Adam are vanity, the sons of men are a lie; in the balances they go up; they are altogether lighter than vanity. David describes the strength of men as vain, for it is nothing before the power of God. The measures of men are also vain, because the true measure is God, not money, or health, or social relationships. Therefore David does not fear those who are hostile to him, because their power is vain, and he is confident in his God, who is able to protect him, and even to restore him to his throne with power.

62.8.0.en: 10- Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.

62.8.1.en: 1- David counsels his people in two matters:

62.8.2.en: a- Not to be attached to the love of money and wealth, because it is vain and does not support a person; rather, strength is from God.

62.8.3.en: b- Not to resort to oppression, because it is a means of coveting the possessions of others and seizing them from them; oppression is a means to unlawful wealth, and this increases God's anger against a person. The Jews were angry with Christ because He drove the sellers out of the Temple, and so prevented their trade and the means of their wealth; for they loved money more than prayer, so much so that they defiled the temple of God with their trading.

62.9.0.en: 11- God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God. 12- Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.

62.9.1.en: 1- David says that God spoke once, meaning that His word is one and does not change. David heard it twice, because God repeats His word many times, so that a person may not forget but may take heed; yet the content of the word is one.

62.9.2.en: 2- God has two essential attributes which must be present in a judge, and they are:

62.9.3.en: a- Power: that is, authority, ability and strength.

62.9.4.en: b- Mercy: that is, compassion and tenderness toward all.

62.9.5.en: For this reason, since God bears these two attributes in perfection, He alone is the Judge of the whole earth, and He will repay every person according to his works on the day of judgment, rewarding the righteous in the Kingdom and punishing the wicked in eternal torment. Neither of the two attributes in God can be neglected, that is, relying on His mercy without fearing Him, so that we become lax toward sin, or fearing His authority and forgetting His mercy, so that we fall into despair.

62.9.6.en: Always remember the fear of God so that you may reject sin, or rise from it quickly if you fall. Remember also His mercy, so that you may be encouraged however much the devil fights you and your weakness appears before him; for your God loves you and has mercy on you, and at the same time protects you by His fear from every sin.

62.9.7.en: Thirst and joys "O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee" (v. 1) Introduction:

62.9.9.en: 2- When it was written: a- When David was fleeing from the face of Absalom in the wilderness of Judah (2 Sam 15:23). This is the more probable opinion, because it mentions that the king rejoices in God (v. 11).

62.9.10.en: b- When David was fleeing from the face of Saul in the wilderness of Judah (1 Sam 23:14), after Samuel had anointed him king, but he had not been proclaimed king over the people because Saul was on the throne.

62.9.11.en: 3- This psalm is a prophecy about the captives in the Assyrian and Babylonian captivity, and those thirsting for God and for worshiping Him in His temple in Jerusalem.

62.9.12.en: 4- This psalm contains a prophecy about the destruction of Saul, or Absalom (v. 9).

62.9.13.en: 5- This psalm suits every person who feels a longing for God and a need to be in His house.

62.9.14.en: 6- The Church prays this psalm at the beginning of every day in the Prime prayer of the Agpeya, because it shows the longings of the praying person for God at the beginning of the day. The Church then prays it again in the prayer of the Sixth Hour, in which Christ said on the cross that He was thirsty, not only for water, but for the salvation of humanity, and humanity answers Him that it is thirsty for His love and His redemption. (1) Longings and praise (vv. 1-7:)

63.0.0.en: 1- O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;

63.0.1.en: 1- David's longings toward God with his soul and body made him wake early to pray. The word for rising early in the original Hebrew means the time of the dawn watch, that is, before daybreak, because David's heart was so occupied with God that he could sleep only a little, and then he would wake up to pray.

63.0.2.en: 2- David was in the wilderness, where there is thirst because there is no water, but the thirst of his soul for God was stronger. When he prayed, his soul was refreshed. His thirst for God was not only for praying in his chamber, but a thirst to be in the presence of God before the ark of the covenant, to offer worship in Jerusalem, for he was far from it because of Absalom.

63.0.3.en: 3- The dry land without water cannot yield fruit, and this is a description of David's soul, which had become dry through its distance from God. The solution is prayer, so that it is refreshed and bears the fruits of the Spirit.

63.1.0.en: 2- To see thy power and thy glory, so as I have seen thee in the sanctuary.

63.1.1.en: 1- As David had experienced seeing God and sensing Him in Jerusalem, when he offered worship in the midst of the crowds before the ark of the covenant, he now longs to see God's power and glory while in the wilderness; for God fills every place, and he is unable to go to Jerusalem and needs God's power and glory, not only to satisfy him, but also to support him against the evil of his enemies. David loves the prayer he was accustomed to in Jerusalem and cannot do without it in any place.

63.1.2.en: 2- When we say that David saw, he expresses his longings to see God's power and glory in His Incarnation, which was to take place in the fullness of time.

63.2.0.en: 3- Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee.

63.2.1.en: 1- David feels that life with God, and enjoying fellowship with Him, is better than all the delights of the life of the world; and likewise, before the greatness of God's mercy, his lips burst forth in praising God and thanking Him. His lips cannot praise God except by His help and mercy.

63.2.2.en: 2- Life with God and the enjoyment of His mercy, even for a short period of life, is better than a long life far from God.

63.2.3.en: 3- Perhaps this verse is a prophecy about the feelings of the captives in Babylon, as they feel that enjoying God's mercy and worshiping Him in Jerusalem is better than all the grandeur of life in Babylon, and there in Jerusalem it is sweet for them to praise before the temple of God.

63.3.0.en: 4- Thus will I bless thee while I live: I will lift up my hands in thy name.

63.3.1.en: 1- Since David enjoyed seeing God and felt His hand supporting him, he declared a clear promise to God to bless Him in his life, meaning throughout his life and in all the times and aspects of his life; for God is the cause of every blessing, success and security in his life.

63.3.2.en: 2- Lifting up the hands is an expression of prayer, supplication and thanksgiving to God, and it is the body's sharing with the spirit in prayer. The lifting up of the hands and the love of prayer are both by the help of God, who encourages us to pray. Indeed, the prayer and the lifting up of the hands are directed to the name of God, that is, His person, because the heart has clung to God and risen to Him along with the body. This shows the extent of David's longings for God, so that they lifted him up to heaven and raised him above many sins because of his preoccupation with the love of God. The lifting up of the hands is also a symbol of victory over Satan, as Moses lifted up his hands and Joshua prevailed over Amalek (Ex 17:11). The lifting up of the hands also means a promise to God that David would continue in prayer, just as God promised His people and lifted up His hand, declaring His promise of the land of Canaan as an inheritance (Ex 6:8).

63.4.0.en: 5- My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips:

63.4.1.en: David declares that just as the body is satisfied with marrow and fatness, so also his soul is satisfied with the richness of divine love, so he blesses God and praises Him with joy. When he prays, his satisfaction and spiritual growth increase, as the body grows by marrow and fatness. Marrow and fatness give food a good taste, and likewise prayer and praise give delight to life; indeed the soul tastes the sweetness of eternity while still on earth, because the whole Kingdom is delight in prayer and praise.

63.5.0.en: 6- When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.

63.5.1.en: Night watches: sleeplessness and inability to sleep.

63.5.2.en: Meditate: I repeat and recite the name of God.

63.5.3.en: 1- David began the psalm by saying that he rises early to pray, because his soul is thirsty for divine love; and he continued all day speaking with God, and when he went in to sleep he kept speaking with God and remembering His name, and when he slept a little from the weariness of the day, he arose and began repeating His holy name, although the dawn had not yet broken. In the Septuagint translation, David awoke in the hours of the night watches; he rose early to God from the time of the dawn watch, while darkness covered the earth and people were asleep, and his heart could not sleep, and he woke to pray and continued until the dawn broke and his day began. Truly David expressed himself when he said, "But I give myself unto prayer" (Ps 109:4).

63.5.4.en: 2- "Upon my bed," that is, in the time of my rest, and "in the night watches," that is, in the time of affliction and sleeplessness, I was praying and meditating on the name of God; for David prays in all circumstances, whether rest or affliction.

63.6.0.en: 7- Because thou hast been my help, therefore in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.

63.6.1.en: David fled from the face of Absalom, and before that from the face of Saul, and God helped him, for He did not allow his pursuers to seize him or kill him. So David felt that he was under God's care and that He was shading him with His wings, and he came to great joy, not only because of God's care, but because he delighted in and was satisfied with the love of God. It may be that God gave him joy by a sense of Him in some way, as it is recorded of the three youths that they saw God in the midst of the furnace, and Daniel saw the angel in the pit (Dan 3:25; 6:22). So David enjoyed fellowship with God, and this is the reason for his joy.

63.6.2.en: If you feel a longing for God, do not delay, but rise to prayer and praise, or read in your Holy Bible and meditate on it, and you will find God clearly and enjoy fellowship with Him, and your heart will rejoice.

63.7.0.en: 8- My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me.

63.7.1.en: 1- From the intensity of David's longings for God he was not content with His care or with seeing Him, but clung to God in love, so that he enjoyed Him continually. And when God saw David's love, He supported him and upheld him with His right hand, that he might remain firm in this love. Whoever seeks God with longing and clings to Him enjoys the power of God, which brings him into the depths of God, so that he experiences inexpressible things, that is, tastes the Kingdom while still on earth.

63.7.2.en: 2- God's right hand signifies Christ, who is the power of God, which appeared in the Incarnation; so whoever seeks God enjoys the salvation and redemption of Christ.

63.8.0.en: 9- But those that seek my soul, to destroy it, shall go into the lower parts of the earth. 10- They are delivered to the hand of the sword; they become the portion of jackals.

63.8.1.en: Jackals: an animal resembling the fox, in size between the fox and the wolf, and it is one of the beasts of prey.

63.8.2.en: 1- After David presented his enjoyment of God as an example of the happiness of the children of God, he presented on the other side the fate of the wicked who want to destroy him, and he defined it in three points:

63.8.3.en: a- They go into the lower parts of the earth, that is, eternal destruction awaits them, and they are cast into hell for their insistence on evil and for killing the innocent such as David.

63.8.4.en: b- They are delivered to the hand of the sword, that is, they perish, and this is destruction on earth, meaning that they perish on earth and in the other life, where there is eternal torment.

63.8.5.en: c- They become portions for jackals: the lion - which signifies Satan - when it attacks a prey kills it, eats part of it and leaves the rest to other beasts of prey, such as jackals. So these wicked men are tormented by Satan, as are the rest of the wicked on earth who attack them; that is, the wicked turn upon one another, and the shame of everyone who follows evil and relies on it appears. Everything that happens to the wicked confirms the faith of the righteous, so they are not troubled by the wrongs of the wicked or their temporary success, because their end is dreadful.

63.9.0.en: 11- But the king shall rejoice in God; every one that sweareth by him shall glory: but the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.

63.9.1.en: 1- David concludes the psalm by saying that the king, that is, David, rejoices in God, to whom he rose early in prayer, and whose fellowship and care he enjoyed. Indeed David becomes an example to others, so the righteous glory because of their faith in God, and their adherence to Him increases, and they swear by His name and not by the names of strange gods; for swearing in the Old Testament was a declaration of a person's faith and his allegiance to God, or to pagan gods. So when God protects David, the righteous who believe in God are confirmed in their faith, and even boast of their God by whom they swear.

63.9.2.en: 2- On the other hand, all the wicked who speak evil, which is lying speech that carries injustice against the innocent, and wrongs that are all temporary and worthless, all this is made void, and God stops the mouths of the wicked when they see God's care and protection of His children, and that the evils of the wicked do not touch the righteous.

63.9.3.en: Contemplate God's work in His saints, and also in His children around you, and your faith will be confirmed and you will grow in your love for God ... Truly the stories of the saints are delightful.

63.9.4.en: God's vengeance for the plots of the wicked. To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. "Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer" (v. 1) Introduction:

63.9.5.en: 1- Its author: David the prophet, as appears from the title of the psalm.

63.9.7.en: a- When David was pursued by Saul, who devised many plots to destroy him.

63.9.8.en: b- When he was pursued from the face of his son Absalom.

63.9.9.en: 3- This psalm is considered a personal lament of David, showing the extent of his suffering, but at the same time his trust and faith in God.

63.9.10.en: 4- This psalm suits every person who is fought by those around him and for whom plots are devised; for this psalm confirms his faith in God.

63.9.11.en: 5- This psalm is considered one of the Messianic psalms, since most of its verses speak of clear events in the life of Christ.

63.9.12.en: 6- This psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
